title: Astaghfirullah, a hundred times
hookLine: asking forgiveness a hundred times a day, as he did (Muslim)

cards: How many times did you say sorry yesterday? Maybe a dozen. Sorry, bumped your cart.
Sorry, running late. Sorry, can you say that again? Most of those aren't really apologies; they're grease on the gears of the day.
How many times did you really ask to be forgiven? Maybe once. Maybe not at all.
In a hadith in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ tells the people: O people, turn to Allah in repentance, for I turn to Him a hundred times a day. A hundred.

teach.b: The word is astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness. Saying it is called istighfar. The root, gh-f-r, means to cover, to shield; Arabic dictionaries list a soldier's helmet, mighfar, from the same root.
So forgiveness, in this picture, isn't just wiping a slate.

It's being covered, protected from what the mistake would otherwise do. Now the surprise. Muslims generally hold that the Prophet was protected from serious sin, though the schools describe that protection differently.
So why ask forgiveness a hundred times a day? Scholars give a few answers. Some say humility: the closer a person is to God, the more they notice the distance.

Some say teaching: he did it so his community would. A version of the hadith says: something covers my heart, a kind of cloud, and I ask forgiveness a hundred times a day. In Bukhari, the number is more than seventy.
And it's not only about sins.
Istighfar is said three times at the end of the prayer, right after the taslim, as if to say: I tried, and it wasn't perfect. The Qur'an adds a promise.
In Surah Nuh, the prophet Nuh tells his people: ask forgiveness of your Lord, and He will send rain, and help you with wealth and sons, and give you gardens and rivers.
Asking forgiveness, paired with rain. There's also a longer form, the master of all istighfar, reported in Bukhari. But the short one, one word, is the one people carry all day.

how: Muslims say astaghfirullah three times right after finishing each prayer, and many repeat it through the day, sometimes a hundred times, following the Prophet's example.

o: a greeting shared after the Friday prayer
asking God to cover and shield a mistake
a quick everyday word for excuse me

games.q: what's inside forgiveness — tap the pairs.

s: istighfar is only for big sins
it's said three times after every prayer, and the Prophet ﷺ said it a hundred times a day.
the root of the word means to cover or shield
the same root gives mighfar, a helmet.
the Prophet said he turned to Allah a hundred times a day
it's in Sahih Muslim; in Bukhari, more than seventy.

games.q: you've just finished the prayer with the peace to both sides. what do many Muslims say first?
games.why: astaghfirullah three times, right after the taslim, as if to say: I tried, and it wasn't perfect.

practice: Rest your right hand, palm up.

If you pray, say astaghfirullah on each finger joint, not rushing, and let a face or a moment come to mind now and then, something you'd like covered; if you don't, say sorry silently on each count, and mean some of them.
Go slowly; you won't reach a hundred, and that's fine.

wordCard.voice: Istighfar. Saying astaghfirullah, I ask Allah's forgiveness; to be covered and shielded, a hundred times a day. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: I ask Allah's forgiveness, from gh-f-r, to cover or shield.

carryVoice: Your line: I ask forgiveness. One word, and a cover. That's day one hundred eighteen.
